title: Free Days Out for Families in the UK, US and Europe
description: Brilliant free days out with kids: free museums, parks, beaches, heritage open days, free museum weekends in the US and free first Sundays in Europe.
h1: Free days out the whole family will love
intro: Dinosaurs, beaches, forests and festivals, all free. Here are the best free family days out at home and abroad, plus the schemes that make paid attractions free for kids.

image.alt: Two parents and a child holding hands on the seashore

blocks.title: Scout’s verdict
blocks.text: Free doesn’t mean second best. The Natural History Museum and the Smithsonian are among the best days out anywhere, and they cost nothing to get in. Budget for the extras instead: travel, parking and the gift shop.

items.title: Natural History Museum

image.alt: The vaulted Hintze Hall at the Natural History Museum, London

items.text: Dinosaurs, a blue whale skeleton and an earthquake room. General admission is free.
saves: General admission is free (some special exhibitions charge)
Book a free timed slot online at busy times
items.scout: The Science Museum and V&A are next door, so you can mix and match one free day.

items.title: Platform 9¾ at King’s Cross

image.alt: A red steam locomotive on a railway line

items.text: A luggage trolley disappearing into the wall at King’s Cross station, with a themed shop next to it. Taking your own photo is free.
saves: Free to visit: you only pay if you want the official photo or shop souvenirs
Go early in the morning to beat the queue
items.scout: A fun free stop on a London day out. Combine it with the free museums in South Kensington.

items.title: Smithsonian museums

image.alt: Visitors exploring a dinosaur fossil gallery

items.text: Most Smithsonian museums on and around the National Mall are free, including Natural History and Air and Space.
saves: Free admission at most Smithsonian museums
Some popular museums use free timed-entry passes: check before you go
items.scout: A whole free holiday in one city! Pick two museums a day max with younger kids.

items.title: US national parks

image.alt: Deer grazing in a meadow below Half Dome in Yosemite

items.text: From Yosemite to the Great Smoky Mountains, America’s national parks are some of the best-value family days out there are.
saves: Fourth graders can get a free Every Kid Outdoors pass for the 2026–27 school year
An annual America the Beautiful pass covers entrance fees at federal sites
Junior Ranger programmes are free at many parks
items.scout: Pick up a Junior Ranger booklet at the visitor centre. Kids love earning the badge.

blocks.title: Schemes that make days out free

items.title: Free child entry at 200+ UK attractions
items.text: Children under 16 who earn a Blue Peter badge get free entry at participating attractions when an adult pays and they show their badge and ID card.
items.terms: Merlin attractions stopped taking badges in 2017. Badges can take weeks to arrive.

items.title: Under-5s go free at most properties
items.text: Both charities let children under 5 in free at most sites, and family memberships can cover the rest of the gang for a year.
items.terms: Check each property: some events and car parks charge extra.

items.merchant: Bank of America Museums on Us
items.title: Free museum entry on the first full weekend of every month
items.text: Bank of America, Merrill and Private Bank cardholders get one free general admission at participating museums. The next weekend is 7–8 November 2026.
items.terms: Cardholder only, no guests. Special exhibitions excluded.

items.title: Free or reduced entry with an EBT card
items.text: Families receiving SNAP benefits can show an EBT card for free or reduced admission at hundreds of participating museums across the US.
items.terms: Rules (group size, price) vary by museum.

items.title: Free national parks pass for fourth graders
items.text: US fourth graders (and home-schooled 10-year-olds) can get a free pass that covers entrance fees for the family at federal lands. The 2026–27 pass runs to 31 August 2027.
items.terms: Covers entrance fees, not camping or tours.

items.title: Free for under-18s at national museums
items.text: France’s national museums, including the Louvre, admit under-18s free. EU/EEA residents aged 18–25 usually go free too.
items.terms: Timed booking is often still required, even for free tickets.

items.title: “Domenica al museo”: free state museums on the first Sunday of the month
items.text: Italian state museums and archaeological sites have opened for free on the first Sunday of the month. Expect crowds and check booking rules.
items.terms: Some sites need advance reservation on free days.

sections.h2: Free days out in the UK
sections.html:
• National museums: general admission is free at the UK’s national museums, including the Natural History Museum, Science Museum, British Museum and Young V&A in London, and the national museums of Scotland and Wales.
  • Heritage Open Days: every September, hundreds of buildings in England that normally charge (or are closed) open for free.
  • Beaches, parks and forests: free to enjoy, though car parks may charge.
  • Blue Peter badge: badge holders under 16 get free entry at 200+ attractions.

sections.h2: Free days out in the US
sections.html:
• Smithsonian museums in Washington, DC are free.
  • Museums on Us: Bank of America cardholders get free museum entry on the first full weekend of each month.
  • Library museum passes: many public libraries lend free or discounted passes to local museums and zoos.
  • National park fee-free days: the National Park Service publishes free-entry days each year. Check nps.gov for the current list.

More in our free US days out guide.

French national museums admit under-18s free, and Italy’s state museums have opened free on the first Sunday of the month. Many cities also have free parks, playgrounds and festivals. Planning a city break? See city breaks on TravelDeals.

faqs.q: What are the best free days out with kids in the UK?
faqs.a: National museums like the Natural History Museum and Science Museum, beaches, country parks, forests and free festivals. Heritage Open Days in September open many paid buildings for free.
Yes. General admission to the national museums is free. Some special exhibitions charge, and some museums ask you to book a free timed ticket at busy times.
